messages.subject: why not qplot(mpg ~wt, data=mtcars)
parts:
hi plotters,

The formula interface supported by R is a great feature for efficient statistical programming*

So I miss it in ggplot2...

Especially when moving back and forth between qplot(x,y) and lm(y~x) or plot(y~x) as the left-right order of DV ~ IV is switched in qplot...

So, how come qplot doesn't support this:

qplot(mpg ~wt, data=mtcars)

Are there barriers to adding a formula= parameter, overriding x,y when !is.na(formula)? Or allow x to be a formula?

t

* FYI, a 1973 paper describing the formula interface. The authors are from Rothamsted, where Fisher worked from 1919!

http://www.jstor.org/discover/10.2307/2346786?uid=3738032&uid=2&uid=4&sid=56261366813

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: why not qplot(mpg ~wt, data=mtcars)
parts:
Hi,

I am ccing the dev list serv too on this. I do not think there is any
reason it could not be done in ggplot2, but I wonder how much it would
add. It is nice for your example: plot(y ~ x), but beyond that, it
struggles a bit, I think. If it were to be added, I thinking drawing
on lattice would be sensible, but even adding | only gets you a
couplel variables and facetting. To map additional variables to
colour, shape, line type, size, etc., I wonder if the formula
interface is complex enough?

In any case, I think it is worth having a discussion about. It would
not even need to be implemented in ggplot2 necessarily. Another
package (such as ggExtra) could upgrade qplot to generic, and define
methods. A (very simple) example showing that it is not difficult to
hack something together to do this:

qplot.formula <- function(formula, ...) {
args <- list(...)
stopifnot(identical(length(formula), 3L))
f <- formula[-1]
p <- do.call("qplot", c(list(x = f[[2]], y = f[[1]]), args))
return(invisible(p))
}

require(ggplot2)
## example 1
p <- qplot.formula(mpg ~ hp, data = mtcars)
print(p)

## can be extend as usual
print(p + stat_smooth())

## example 2
p2 <- qplot.formula(y ~ x, data = diamonds)
print(p2)

## works with variables in the global environment too
y <- mtcars$mpg
x <- mtcars$hp
p3 <- qplot.formula(y ~ x)
print(p3)

## lattice for demonstration
require(lattice)
xyplot(mpg ~ hp, data = mtcars)
xyplot(mpg ~ hp | cyl, data = mtcars)

How much demand is there for a formula interface? Would people just
want it in qplot? Part of me thinks that would just add confusion
between working with qplot and ggplot if one accepts formulae and the
other does not. On the other hand, a simple formula interface may
ease new comers to ggplot2, as qplot already does, but it would follow
fairly sensibly then from any introduction of most basic modelling
functions.

f <- mpg ~ factor(cyl)

p4 <- qplot.formula(f, data = mtcars, geom = c("boxplot", "jitter"))
print(p4)

summary(lm(f, data = mtcars))

Cheers,

Josh
